values.goal: Design GSAP motion that remains stable as timing, layout, and input change.
values.capstone: Integrate keyboard access, reduced motion, and cleanup paths into learning-stage guidance, and write a verification report.

values.title: Starting and target values
values.prerequisites: Prepare the Tween and playhead exercise results from Unit 1, “Tween and Timeline”.
values.concepts.0.title: What from and to leave implicit
values.concepts.0.explanation: x is the element’s horizontal translation transform value, compared in px in this unit. For a card initially at x=40, gsap.to(card, { x: 240 }) moves from the current value to 240. gsap.from(card, { x: -80 }) starts at -80 and returns to the original value 40. gsap.fromTo(card, { x: -80 }, { x: 240 }) specifies both values explicitly, so the original 40 is not an endpoint of the movement. To compare the three APIs, create a separate card for each and initialize all of them to 40. Running them sequentially on one card makes the previous tween’s end value the next tween’s current value, changing the comparison conditions.
values.concepts.1.title: The built-in example runs a single fromTo path
values.concepts.1.explanation: The default built-in example’s Run experiment button is not a to/from selector. Before a click, x has not been set and the card is at x=0. On the first click, reverse changes from false to true and creates gsap.fromTo(box, { x: 240, opacity: 0.2 }, { x: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 1, immediateRender: false }). The next click starts at x=0 and ends at x=240. The first run therefore moves from 240 on the right back to the original position. The output text is guidance defined in the code, rather than a measurement log continuously reading the current coordinates.
values.concepts.2.title: Initial application separates creation from the first render
values.concepts.2.explanation: For from and fromTo, immediateRender defaults to true, applying the starting values on creation. Specifying immediateRender: false preserves the original styles between tween creation and the first render. Put this option in the target settings, the third argument to fromTo. The built-in example creates the tween itself on a click, preserving the appearance before that click. Even if x=0 immediately after the first click’s synchronous code, playback moves from the specified starting value x=240, so a jump may be visible. Do not interpret immediateRender: false as smoothly continuing from the current position. Compare the role of to if you want to start from the current position.
values.concepts.3.title: A minimal experiment comparing the three APIs under the same conditions
values.concepts.4.title: Calculate the controlled experiment’s expected table first
values.concepts.4.explanation: For the code above, the expected x at before is 40 for all three cards. At created, expect to=40, from=-80, fromTo=-80, because the from APIs retain their default initial application. At half, expect to=140, from=-20, fromTo=80; at end, expect to=240, from=40, fromTo=240. For example, the midpoint of to is 40 + (240 - 40) × 0.5 = 140. These numbers are predictions calculated from the code’s conditions. After running, save each output row as an actual observation. For rows that differ from the predictions, also record the initial value, API, ease, and progress settings.
values.concepts.5.title: Values verified in the built-in example and the scope of verification
values.concepts.5.explanation: Verification of the existing example’s mount on a local Vite page in HeadlessChrome 151.0.7922.34 confirmed initial x=0 and x=0 immediately after the first click’s synchronous code. After forcing progress(1) on the first tween, it read x=0 and opacity=1; after progress(1) on the second tween, it read x=240. At progress(0.5), it read x=60 and opacity=0.8; the default example does not specify ease. This record contains property values checked by directly moving GSAP’s progress. The three-card code above was also run in the same browser, confirming that x at before, created, half, and end matched the expected table. With immediateRender: false added, created was 40 for all three cards, and half and end still matched the original table. This record does not measure actual natural-playback duration or whether the screen flickers. The reproduction code is in [Representative lesson browser checks](../../../../../../tests/browser/representative-lessons.js).
values.concepts.6.title: Failure cases that produce unexpected results
values.concepts.6.explanation: Creating to, from, and fromTo in succession on the same card can make multiple tweens write the same property or read styles left by a previous run. Use separate comparison cards and reset the initial values before each run. On each new click, the built-in example kills the existing tween and creates a new fromTo. Do not use it as an experiment in preserving the current position during rapid clicks. Also, expecting progress(0.5) to mean half the distance with the default ease leads to an incorrect comparison. Only the separate experiment above controls ease with ease: 'none'. Put duration in fromTo’s third, target object rather than its starting object, and check the expected direction and actual end value first.
values.concepts.7.title: Repeat the experiment changing only initial application
values.concepts.7.explanation: Add immediateRender: false to options in the three-card experiment and run it again. In the paused state’s created rows, from and fromTo are now expected to retain the original x=40 too. Directly setting progress(0.5) and progress(1) moves to those points, so the expected half and end values remain unchanged. This comparison checks the styles immediately after creation separately from the movement interval. To visually check flicker in the initial screen, define automatic-playback and delay conditions in a separate experiment and observe again. Do not claim to have observed the screen’s first paint based only on a paused progress table.

values.outcomes.1: Output: a transform table immediately after creation and after completion. Connect your explanation of initial application to the code.
